decisions.title: CA-ST-1: V2 persistent character, persona, note, and lorebook effects remain explicit no-ops
decisions.baselineBehavior: The baseline executed V2 persistent character, persona, note, and lorebook effects.
decisions.decidedBehavior: Fastify preserves imported definitions but does not execute those persistent mutations; editor notices and runtime warnings make the boundary visible.
observables: V2 persistent character, persona, note, and lorebook effects remain explicit no-ops
decisions.rationale: The maintainer individually declined this unsafe persistence port on 2026-08-02.
decisions.parityAlternative: Restore the baseline behavior described for CA-ST-1.
diagnostics: The unsupported boundary must be hidden, rejected, or visibly diagnosed; silent partial behavior is forbidden.
decisions.revisitTrigger: Revisit only with a separately designed durable, permissioned mutation contract.

decisions.title: CA-ST-2: V1/V2 command and privileged effect families remain explicit no-ops
decisions.baselineBehavior: The baseline could execute command and privileged trigger effect families without the Fastify permission boundary.
decisions.decidedBehavior: Fastify keeps the definitions inert and surfaces their unsupported status.
observables: V1/V2 command and privileged effect families remain explicit no-ops
decisions.rationale: The same 2026-08-02 maintainer decision declined the privileged effect port.
decisions.parityAlternative: Restore the baseline behavior described for CA-ST-2.
diagnostics: The unsupported boundary must be hidden, rejected, or visibly diagnosed; silent partial behavior is forbidden.
decisions.revisitTrigger: Revisit only with an explicit permission and durable-effect design.

decisions.title: D1: Whole-database portable exports retain credentials with a mandatory warning
decisions.baselineBehavior: Whole-database exports included inline provider credentials without a dedicated warning.
decisions.decidedBehavior: The whole-database export remains secret-bearing and requires a user-facing handling warning.
observables: Whole-database portable exports retain credentials with a mandatory warning
decisions.rationale: The maintainer chose keep-and-warn rather than a new content-only format before beta.
decisions.parityAlternative: Restore the baseline behavior described for D1.
diagnostics: The owning workflow and regression evidence expose the decided outcome.
decisions.revisitTrigger: Revisit when a content-only portable export flavor is designed.

decisions.title: D2: Stale inline model-profile secrets are scrubbed without minting credentials
decisions.baselineBehavior: The fork-point baseline had no modelProfiles, so it had no equivalent inline profile-secret restore path.
decisions.decidedBehavior: Fastify scrubs stale inline profile secrets; legacy scalar keys still mint credentials, but pre-credential-store fork-native profile secrets do not.
observables: Stale inline model-profile secrets are scrubbed without minting credentials
decisions.rationale: The maintainer accepted the bounded pre-beta population and retained the destructive scrub.
decisions.parityAlternative: Restore the baseline behavior described for D2.
diagnostics: The owning workflow and regression evidence expose the decided outcome.
decisions.revisitTrigger: Reopen if a pre-beta build containing inline model-profile secrets was distributed to another user.

decisions.title: CA-OR-2: Group-chat generation remains no-port
decisions.baselineBehavior: The baseline supported group-chat generation and resolved group-aware CBS callbacks through the last speaking member.
decisions.decidedBehavior: Fastify does not expose or execute group-chat generation, and retired group-aware parser branches do not resolve an imported group through a member character.
observables: Group-chat generation remains no-port
CBS parsing does not revive group-member resolution through imported legacy group-shaped data.
decisions.rationale: The maintainer removed the remaining legacy group-chat UI branches, kept the server and browser hard-fail defenses, and described group chat as fully legacy because the server has no group/member model.
decisions.parityAlternative: Restore the baseline behavior described for CA-OR-2.
diagnostics: The unsupported boundary must be hidden, rejected, or visibly diagnosed; silent partial behavior is forbidden.
decisions.revisitTrigger: Revisit only after a separate group-chat product decision.

decisions.title: CA-PR-3: Non-server-routable providers remain unavailable

decisions.rationale: The maintainer documented these browser/local selectors as explicitly rejected by server dispatch even when the shared registry can describe them.
decisions.parityAlternative: Restore the baseline behavior described for CA-PR-3.
diagnostics: The unsupported boundary must be hidden, rejected, or visibly diagnosed; silent partial behavior is forbidden.
decisions.revisitTrigger: Revisit when one of these providers gains an authenticated server execution design.

decisions.title: cluster-15: Per-key script conflict fencing remains while local lore merges per entry
decisions.baselineBehavior: The baseline used last-writer-wins script writes.
decisions.decidedBehavior: Fastify retains per-key conflict fencing, but the coarse whole-array lore conflict was fixed to a per-entry semantic merge.
observables: Per-key script conflict fencing remains while local lore merges per entry
decisions.rationale: The maintainer approved the narrow merge fix and retained the surrounding data-loss fence.
decisions.parityAlternative: Restore the baseline behavior described for cluster-15.
diagnostics: The owning workflow and regression evidence expose the decided outcome.

decisions.title: upstream-F1: Character and module interchangeability remains unported
decisions.baselineBehavior: Post-fork upstream added character-module conversion and CharX module interchange.
decisions.decidedBehavior: Fastify does not expose or partially execute the conversion surface.
observables: Character and module interchangeability remains unported
decisions.rationale: The maintainer explicitly accepted that upstream CharX module exports will not import because the feature is rarely used, with a user-pain revisit trigger.
decisions.parityAlternative: Restore the baseline behavior described for upstream-F1.
diagnostics: The unsupported boundary must be hidden, rejected, or visibly diagnosed; silent partial behavior is forbidden.
decisions.revisitTrigger: Revisit if users report module-format interoperability pain.

decisions.title: upstream-81b: Dynamic OpenAI model registration remains unported
decisions.baselineBehavior: Post-fork upstream can register arbitrary OpenAI models dynamically.
decisions.decidedBehavior: Fastify retains a curated provider catalog.
observables: Dynamic OpenAI model registration remains unported
decisions.rationale: The maintainer explicitly chose the curated catalog rather than adding provider-operation and credential plumbing for dynamic OpenAI registration.
decisions.parityAlternative: Restore the baseline behavior described for upstream-81b.
diagnostics: The unsupported boundary must be hidden, rejected, or visibly diagnosed; silent partial behavior is forbidden.
decisions.revisitTrigger: Revisit if users request unlisted OpenAI models.

decisions.title: Responsive navigation uses the shared App shell
decisions.baselineBehavior: The baseline conditionally mounted MobileHeader, MobileBody, and MobileFooter when betaMobileGUI was enabled at a narrow viewport or in lite mode.
decisions.decidedBehavior: Fastify keeps those legacy components unmounted and uses the shared App sidebar/dialog shell for responsive navigation and chat.
observables: Narrow viewports retain the live route, sidebar, chat, focus, Escape, and mutation controls through the shared responsive shell rather than the legacy beta-mobile component tree.
decisions.rationale: The maintainer explicitly removed tests for the unmounted legacy shell and documented the mounted App plus responsive Chromium journeys as the current product contract.
decisions.parityAlternative: Restore betaMobileGUI selection and mount the baseline MobileHeader, MobileBody, and MobileFooter component tree.
diagnostics: The live responsive shell exposes a stable marker and owns modal focus trapping, Escape, sidebar, and chat controls; unmounted legacy controls cannot be advertised as supported.
decisions.revisitTrigger: Revisit if a separately designed mobile-only shell is mounted in production again.

decisions.title: Character additional-information editing and retrieval remain retired
decisions.baselineBehavior: The baseline exposed an additional-information editor, split Character.additionalText into paragraph blocks, selected the top three embedding-similar blocks from recent chat context, and inserted the result into the character description before personality and scenario.
decisions.decidedBehavior: Fastify preserves imported additionalText but keeps editing retired behind a read-only unsupported notice and omits the field from model-visible prompt assembly.
observables: Nonempty imported additionalText remains stored and visible as unsupported compatibility data, no editor is exposed, and none of the field reaches prompt rows or provider-ready messages.
Empty additionalText exposes neither an editor nor the imported-data notice.
decisions.rationale: The maintainer explicitly retired the partially disconnected editor and embedding retrieval boundary, preserving imported data and diagnosing the unsupported field rather than silently accepting edits that do not affect generation.
decisions.parityAlternative: Restore the character editor and baseline embedding-ranked additional-information insertion before model dispatch.
diagnostics: Nonempty imported data surfaces a read-only unsupported notice; the prompt regression fails if the compatibility data enters any generated prompt row.
decisions.revisitTrigger: Revisit if server-owned embedding retrieval is restored with an explicit authoring, persistence, prompt-budget, and provider-visible contract.

decisions.title: CBS history arguments select bounded recent-message windows
decisions.baselineBehavior: The baseline ignored every history/messages argument and returned the full transcript.
decisions.decidedBehavior: A positive integer argument returns that many recent messages, while an invalid argument returns an empty array and an omitted argument retains the full transcript.
observables: {{history::N}} and {{messages::N}} select the N most recent messages in transcript order.
Missing, valid, zero, negative, and invalid window arguments remain distinct.
decisions.rationale: The maintainer deliberately introduced numeric CBS history windows as an explicit parser feature.
decisions.parityAlternative: Ignore the argument and return every transcript message as the fork-point baseline did.
diagnostics: Shared fixtures pin omitted, valid, and invalid argument outcomes at baseline, browser, and Fastify consumers.

decisions.title: CBS reverse operates on its expanded argument
decisions.baselineBehavior: The baseline reversed the raw matcher text, so {{reverse::abc}} produced cba::esrever.
decisions.decidedBehavior: The reverse callback operates on its expanded argument, so {{reverse::abc}} produces cba.
observables: The matcher name and separator are never included in reverse output.
Argument expansion occurs before reversal.
decisions.rationale: The maintainer explicitly repaired the callback to reverse the supplied value rather than parser syntax.
decisions.parityAlternative: Restore raw matcher-text reversal, including the matcher name and separator.
decisions.source: commit 16842f066c32ce6474469e92c9b303bdd62ec6b3 (fix: repair CBS reverse and setdefaultvar null handling)
diagnostics: The shared baseline-drift fixture preserves both exact outputs and prevents normalization from hiding the change.

decisions.title: CBS metadata reports the Fastify-only runtime contract
decisions.baselineBehavior: The baseline reported risutype=web and rejected the fastify metadata key while retaining desktop-era local/node branches.
decisions.decidedBehavior: The sole-platform runtime reports risutype=fastify and fastify=1; retired local/node metadata remain false and browser language comes from the request context.
observables: Runtime metadata identifies Fastify instead of the retired web/desktop split.
Local, node, Fastify, Risu type, and language values have the same explicit browser and server context ownership.
decisions.rationale: The maintainer removed desktop/Tauri authority, collapsed the runtime contract, made Fastify the sole platform, and later made browser-context CBS ownership explicit.
decisions.parityAlternative: Report the baseline web/desktop metadata values and reject the Fastify key.
diagnostics: Unsupported or unavailable server callback context is reported through prompt diagnostics instead of silently impersonating a retired platform.
decisions.revisitTrigger: Revisit if another supported runtime becomes a product target.

decisions.title: Standalone CBS slot tags resolve prompt-agent context
decisions.baselineBehavior: The baseline documented slot but left a standalone {{slot::name}} tag literal outside legacy each substitution.
decisions.decidedBehavior: Standalone slot tags resolve named values from the parser context so prompt-agent slot injection is executable.
observables: A supplied slot value replaces its standalone tag.
Legacy each-loop slot substitution retains source order and nesting behavior.
decisions.rationale: The maintainer introduced the context agent with flexible prompt-slot injection and made the previously documentation-only callback executable.
decisions.parityAlternative: Leave standalone slot tags literal and restrict slot replacement to the baseline each-loop substitution.
decisions.source: commit c080398396d8bc7b6ca5322280c1e0b47dad78cd (feat: introduce context agent for flexible prompt slot injection)
diagnostics: Unknown callbacks remain literal; a supplied slot context is required for standalone replacement.

decisions.title: CBS each expansion has a fail-closed element budget
decisions.baselineBehavior: The baseline expanded arbitrarily large {{#each}} arrays without an element cap.
decisions.decidedBehavior: Each expansion stops before output construction when more than 4096 elements are requested and surfaces a typed parser-budget error through every recursive call.
observables: Arrays of at most 4096 elements preserve ordered substitution.
An over-budget expansion fails visibly and cannot continue with partial parser output.
decisions.rationale: The maintainer explicitly capped each expansion and later repaired recursion-budget propagation so nested parsing cannot bypass the limit.
decisions.parityAlternative: Permit unbounded each expansion as the baseline did.
diagnostics: RisuParserBudgetError includes the requested and maximum element counts.
decisions.revisitTrigger: Revisit only with an equivalent bounded streaming expansion design.

decisions.title: Fastify Lua edit-hook failures surface instead of returning unchanged content
decisions.baselineBehavior: The baseline browser edit hook caught a Lua failure and returned the original content.
decisions.decidedBehavior: The browser fallback remains baseline-compatible, while server-owned prompt execution throws a sanitized Lua failure so generation cannot silently continue with unchanged content.
observables: Browser-only Lua edit execution retains the original content after a failure.
Fastify-owned Lua edit execution fails visibly before provider dispatch rather than silently applying the original content.
decisions.rationale: The maintainer explicitly surfaced silent trigger fallbacks while preserving the legacy browser fallback for client-owned execution.
decisions.parityAlternative: Catch the server Lua error and continue generation with unchanged content.
decisions.source: commit ccfc708189cb95c5f3aa28321dc03383ccb0550c (fix: surface silent trigger fallbacks)
diagnostics: The Fastify failure includes its edit mode and sanitized script failure; browser fallback behavior is pinned separately.
